case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses how Bluetooth SIG qualification applies to derivative products, rebranded products, and products with hardware or software modifications. The customer asks whether multiple model names, different sellers, or minor design changes require new Bluetooth qualification work. The consultant explains how Product List additions, existing QDID reuse, and qualification ownership work under Bluetooth SIG rules. The discussion also clarifies the scope of Bluetooth qualification versus non-Bluetooth product changes and explains how ICS-defined functionality determines reuse eligibility.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The consultant explains that derivative products using the same Bluetooth SoC or module, host stack, and Bluetooth functionality can typically reuse an existing qualification through Product List addition. The thread clarifies that qualification responsibility belongs to the company selling or branding the product, even if the hardware manufacturer remains unchanged. The discussion distinguishes Bluetooth-related changes from unrelated hardware or software changes, noting that RF-impacting modifications such as antenna changes still require verification against the original qualification class and RF limits. The consultant also explains that Bluetooth qualification decisions are based on detailed ICS-defined functionality and Support Layers, not only visible profile names or feature summaries.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The core decision logic is whether the Bluetooth Support Layers, ICS-defined functionality, or RF characteristics of the qualified design have changed. If the Bluetooth implementation remains unchanged, the existing qualified design can typically be reused through Product List addition. If the branded selling entity changes, that company must complete its own qualification registration even when the hardware is identical. RF-impacting modifications must still satisfy the conditions of the original qualification before reuse is allowed.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly treating a modified Bluetooth implementation as a derivative product could invalidate qualification eligibility and create Bluetooth SIG compliance problems. Failing to qualify products under the correct selling company could violate Bluetooth trademark and licensing requirements. Improper handling of antenna or RF-path changes could unintentionally alter BR/EDR class compliance and require additional qualification work. Misunderstanding ICS-defined functionality could also lead to incorrect assumptions about qualification reuse and unnecessary testing or listing errors.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Bluetooth qualification reuse decisions should always be based on the detailed qualified Bluetooth implementation, including ICS-defined functionality, Support Layers, RF behavior, and qualification ownership rules, rather than only visible product similarities or profile summaries.
